ui_bugs.issue: Handoff expects a practice rival to take the seat in ~5-7 s if no human is free. Measured 15.83 s from tap-to-card-1 in E5 (no human was available; practice rival Avni N. seated). The 'Finding a rival…' spinner stays visible significantly longer than the handoff target. The WS does open promptly, so the delay is on the server bot-seat trigger or the client's wait window. Repro: rf-chapter-picker -> rf-scope-pcm -> rf-scope-count-30 -> rf-scope-play, measure time until duel-card appears. Screenshot: /app/test_reports/artifacts_iter121/e6_searching.jpeg. Suggested check: /app/backend/duels.py around make_bot / seat_duel / quick-match wait timer — confirm the bot-fallback fires at the 5-7 s mark, not later.

On some cards the verdict chip (duel-verdict) disappears before a UI poll of ~0.15 s intervals can read it — in E1, 5 out of 30 cards returned null for the chip text even though the server outcome field was populated. For the TIME-UP card (card 25) the verdict was also missed. This is a minor automation/UX observation: the chip may be hidden too quickly after SKIPPED/TIME UP (handoff notes the verdict stays ~1.1 s after an answer, ~0.7 s after skip/time-out, so TIME UP falls in the short window). Suggest keeping verdict visible for the same ~1.1 s on every outcome type for consistency.

critical_code_review_comments: backend/duels.py render() correctly strips 'answer', 'explain', 'formula' from each card and rewrites card id to d.id[:8]-k when d.status != 'finished' (lines 548-552). public_card_dict leaves those keys in the dict, but render() is the only path that ships cards to the client in both HTTP (view) and WS (notify/pusher via render(with_cards=...)). So the fairness guarantee is driven by the single 'reveal' flag being tied to status == 'finished' — a reasonable, centralised check.

frontend/app/rapid/duel.tsx exit sheet: duel-exit-confirm fires POST /duels/<id>/forfeit and navigates back regardless of the response (catch(() => {})). Acceptable, because the pusher will reconcile; but a failed forfeit will leave the match in 'ready' state on the server until it times out. Minor.

frontend/src/rapid/MatchResult.tsx duel-toggle-misses iterates missed cards — the screenshot shows the right answer highlighted per missed card and the explanation beneath; this correctly uses the reveal-enabled card payload only after the match finishes.
